e-15602.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
e-15602.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083350/assets/a664a3af1ba466491d209dadd32a3be026a5179ac2d0281b55f30917f9ab016b.png)
What would be the vector equation of the line?
e-15602.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2+2t \\ 5t \\ 1-t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2t \\ 5t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

e-15603.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Parallel To a Straight Line Given Parametrically
e-15603.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083350/assets/f161e07945eb3fe2350a56ab5cb96fa0ae2d055eb3b4cc633abfae30839ec76f.png)
Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
e-15603.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5-t \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-t \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

This implies that the line passes through the point $(5,3,1)$ and is parallel to the vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083350/assets/11701a2d63851a3f241d8bd905693abaaa6eda6fe4ba0c5710c92d8189595ffd.png)

e-15604.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equations of a Line
e-15604.problem:
Find the parametric equations of the line shown in the figure below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083350/assets/53386f04f4025fda6ab579113a8ecb53a19f4dc0a77903adc05bac3a71429717.png)
e-15604.worked_solution:
We know that the line passes through the points $P(3,3,-5)$ and $Q(1,0,-1)$. Now, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ -5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ -5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2t \\ -3t \\ 4t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3-2t \\ 3-3t \\ -5+4t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$ And finally, the parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3-2t \\ y=3-3t \\ z=-5+4t\end{aligned}
$$

e-15605.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equations of a Segment
e-15605.problem: Find the parametric equations that describe all the points on the line segment $\overline{PQ},$ where $P(1,-5,3)$ and $Q(0, 4, -4).$
e-15605.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the line passing through the given points. We can use the vector $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ -4\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 9 \\ -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 9 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-t \\ 9t \\ -7t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1-t \\ -5+9t \\ 3-7t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$ 

To get the equations for the line segment, we take only $t \in [0,1].$ Notice that substitution of $t=0$ in the above equation gives the coordinates of $P$ and substitution of $t=1$ gives the coordinates of $Q.$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the line segment $\overline{PQ}$ are the following:

before.html:
Question 1
?

Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: {x=−3y=5tz=−2 What would be the vector equation of the line?

a
r=[−20−3]+t[050],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=[30−2]+t[150],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[302]+t[050],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=[−30−2]+t[050],t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=[−302]+t[0−5−5],t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit

decision.explanation: Separating the constant coordinates from the coefficients of t gives r=(-3,0,-2)+t(0,5,0), which reproduces x=-3, y=5t, and z=-2. Thus option d is correct.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-3 \\ y=5t \\ z=-2\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
after.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5t \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-3 \\ y=5t \\ z=-2\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
content.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5t \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Question 2
?

Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: {x=5y=4tz=7 What would be the vector equation of the line?

a
r=[040]+t[507],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=t[040],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=t[507],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
None of the listed
e
r=[507]+t[040],t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit

decision.explanation: The constant coordinates give the position vector (5,0,7), and the coefficients of t give the direction vector (0,4,0). Option e therefore reproduces x=5, y=4t, and z=7.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5 \\ y=4t \\ z=7\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
after.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 4t \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5 \\ y=4t \\ z=7\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
content.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 4t \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

before.html:
Question 3
?

Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: {x=1+ty=2−tz=0 What would be the vector equation of the line?

a
r=t[1−10],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=[120]+t[1−10],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=t[120],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=[1−10]+t[120],t∈(−∞,∞)
e
None of the listed
Submit

decision.explanation: Separating constants and coefficients of t gives r=(1,2,0)+t(1,-1,0). Its coordinates are (1+t,2-t,0), exactly the given equations, so option b is correct.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+t \\ y=2-t \\ z=0\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
after.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1+t \\ 2-t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}t \\ -t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+t \\ y=2-t \\ z=0\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
content.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1+t \\ 2-t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}t \\ -t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Question 4
?

Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: {x=13−8ty=7tz=−7−3t What would be the vector equation of the line?

a
r=[−1307]+t[−8−73],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=[130−7]+t[−37−8],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[130−7]+t[−87−3],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=[130−7]+t[−8−73],t∈(−∞,∞)
e
r=[1307]+t[873],t∈(−∞,∞)
Submit

decision.explanation: The constant terms form (13,0,-7), and the coefficients of t form (-8,7,-3). Thus option c gives coordinates (13-8t,7t,-7-3t), matching all three equations.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=13-8t \\ y=7t \\ z=-7-3t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
after.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}13-8t \\ 7t \\ -7-3t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}13 \\ 0 \\ -7\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-8t \\ 7t \\ -3t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}13 \\ 0 \\ -7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 7 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}13 \\ 0 \\ -7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 7 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=13-8t \\ y=7t \\ z=-7-3t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
content.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}13-8t \\ 7t \\ -7-3t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}13 \\ 0 \\ -7\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-8t \\ 7t \\ -3t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}13 \\ 0 \\ -7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 7 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}13 \\ 0 \\ -7\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 7 \\ -3\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

before.html:
Question 5
?

Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations: {x=5y=2+3tz=−t What would be the vector equation of the line?

a
r=[520]+t[03−1],t∈(−∞,∞)
b
r=t[520],t∈(−∞,∞)
c
r=[03−1]+t[520],t∈(−∞,∞)
d
r=t[03−1],t∈(−∞,∞)
e
None of the listed
Submit

decision.explanation: The constant terms give (5,2,0), and the coefficients of t give (0,3,-1). Option a therefore has coordinates (5,2+3t,-t), matching the given equations.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5 \\ y=2+3t \\ z=-t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
after.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2+3t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=5 \\ y=2+3t \\ z=-t\end{aligned}
$$

What would be the vector equation of the line?
content.worked_solution:
These parametric equations are equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2+3t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=t-1 \\ y=-t+1 \\ z=-t-1\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
after.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}t-1 \\ -t+1 \\ -t-1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}t \\ -t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$  

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-1,1,-1)$   and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Parallel To a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=t-1 \\ y=-t+1 \\ z=-t-1\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
content.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}t-1 \\ -t+1 \\ -t-1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}t \\ -t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$  

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-1,1,-1)$   and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$  

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-1,1,-1)$   and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3t-3 \\ y=7-9t \\ z=\frac{3}{2}t-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
after.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3t-3 \\ 7-9t \\ \frac{3}{2}t-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 7 \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ -9t \\ \frac{3}{2}t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 7 \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 7 \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-3,7,-\frac{1}{2})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}].$

EXPLANATION

First, let's find the corresponding vector equation: [xyz]=[3t−37−9t32t−12][xyz]=[−37−12]+[3t−9t32t][xyz]=[−37−12]+t[3−932]r=[−37−12]+t[3−932], where t∈(−∞,∞).

This implies that the straight line passes through the point (−3,7,−12) and is parallel to the vector v=[3−932].

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms the direction vector (3,-9,3/2), obtained from the coefficients of t, so option a is correct. Option b is not a scalar multiple: negating the direction vector would give (-3,9,-3/2), not (-3,9,-1/2).

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Parallel To a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=3t-3 \\ y=7-9t \\ z=\frac{3}{2}t-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
content.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3t-3 \\ 7-9t \\ \frac{3}{2}t-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 7 \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ -9t \\ \frac{3}{2}t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 7 \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 7 \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-3,7,-\frac{1}{2})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -9 \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}].$

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+3t \\ y=2-4t \\ z=2+t\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
after.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1+3t \\ 2-4t \\ 2+t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ -4t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the line passes through the point $(1,2,2)$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+3t \\ y=2-4t \\ z=2+t\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
content.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1+3t \\ 2-4t \\ 2+t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ -4t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

This implies that the line passes through the point $(1,2,2)$ and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=\frac{1}{3}t-2 \\ y=5-4t \\ z=2t+\frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Parallel To a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=\frac{1}{3}t-2 \\ y=5-4t \\ z=2t+\frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
content.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}t-2 \\ 5-4t \\ 2t+\frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ \frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}t \\ -4t \\ 2t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ \frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ \frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$  

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-2,5,\frac{1}{7})$  and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2t+1 \\ y=3-t \\ z=t+2\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
after.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2t+1 \\ 3-t \\ t+2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2t \\ -t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$  

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(1,3,2)$  and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Parallel To a Straight Line Given Parametrically
content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2t+1 \\ y=3-t \\ z=t+2\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
content.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2t+1 \\ 3-t \\ t+2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2t \\ -t \\ t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$  

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(1,3,2)$  and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Question 11
?

Find the parametric equations of the line shown in the figure above.

a
{x=4−ty=−3+tz=−2+4t
b
{x=3−ty=−2+tz=2+4t
c
{x=4ty=−3tz=−2t
d
{x=−1+4ty=1−3tz=4−2t
e
{x=−ty=tz=4t
Submit

decision.explanation: Using P=(-1,1,4) and Q=(3,-2,2), the direction vector Q-P is (4,-3,-2). Thus (x,y,z)=(-1,1,4)+t(4,-3,-2), matching option d and giving P at t=0 and Q at t=1.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083350/assets/58076d96d149ff4521103fd15c7187bc1a58595ab20f28be92be0f79385aee61.png)

Find the parametric equations of the line shown in the figure above.
after.worked_solution:
We know that the line passes through the points $P(-1,1,4)$ and $Q(3,-2,2).$ Now, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$,  as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ -3t \\ -2t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1+4t \\ 1-3t \\ 4-2t\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ Therefore, the parametric equations are:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-1+4t \\ y=1-3t \\ z=4-2t\end{aligned}
$$

a
{x=4−ty=−3+tz=−2+4t
b

{x=4ty=−3tz=−2t

{x=−1+4ty=1−3tz=4−2t
e
{x=−ty=tz=4t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We know that the line passes through the points P(−1,1,4) and Q(3,−2,2). Now, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector PQ→, as follows:

v=PQ→=OQ→−OP→=[3−22]−[−114]=[4−3−2]

So, the vector equation of the line is

r=p+tvr=[−114]+t[4−3−2][xyz]=[−114]+[4t−3t−2t][xyz]=[−1+4t1−3t4−2t],

where t∈(−∞,∞). Therefore, the parametric equations are: {x=−1+4ty=1−3tz=4−2t

content.worked_solution:
We know that the line passes through the points $P(-1,1,4)$ and $Q(3,-2,2).$ Now, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$,  as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ -3t \\ -2t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1+4t \\ 1-3t \\ 4-2t\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ Therefore, the parametric equations are:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-1+4t \\ y=1-3t \\ z=4-2t\end{aligned}
$$

Question 12
?

Find the parametric equations of the line shown in the figure above.

a
{x=−ty=3tz=2t
b
{x=3ty=tz=3t
c
{x=−1+3ty=3+tz=2+3t
d
{x=2−ty=4+3tz=5+2t
e
{x=3−ty=1+3tz=3+2t
Submit

decision.explanation: The direction vector is Q-P=(2-(-1),4-3,5-2)=(3,1,3). Starting at P=(-1,3,2) gives x=-1+3t, y=3+t, z=2+3t, matching option c.

after.name: Question 12
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083350/assets/1ffc0945ea74b1bd467a0b9935ee28b88be004c18b11492d67ecdfec56e1bb09.png)

Find the parametric equations of the line shown in the figure above.
after.worked_solution:
We know that the line passes through the points $P(-1,3,2)$ and $Q(2,4,5).$ Now, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ t \\ 3t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1+3t \\ 3+t \\ 2+3t\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ And finally, the parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-1+3t \\ y=3+t \\ z=2+3t\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

We know that the line passes through the points P(−1,3,2) and Q(2,4,5). Now, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector PQ→ as follows:

v=PQ→=OQ→−OP→=[245]−[−132]=[313]

So, the vector equation of the line is

r=p+tvr=[−132]+t[313][xyz]=[−132]+[3tt3t][xyz]=[−1+3t3+t2+3t],

where t∈(−∞,∞). And finally, the parametric equations: {x=−1+3ty=3+tz=2+3t

content.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14083350/assets/1ffc0945ea74b1bd467a0b9935ee28b88be004c18b11492d67ecdfec56e1bb09.png)

Find the parametric equations of the line shown in the figure above.
content.worked_solution:
We know that the line passes through the points $P(-1,3,2)$ and $Q(2,4,5).$ Now, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 5\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3t \\ t \\ 3t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1+3t \\ 3+t \\ 2+3t\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ And finally, the parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-1+3t \\ y=3+t \\ z=2+3t\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The direction vector Q-P is (4,-1,2). Starting at P gives x=1+4t, y=4-t, z=-2+2t, matching option c. These equations give P at t=0 and Q at t=1.

after.name: Question 13
after.problem: Find the parametric equations of the line that passes through the points $P(1,4,-2)$ and $Q(5,3,0).$
after.worked_solution:
We know that the line passes through the points $P(1,4,-2)$ and $Q(5,3,0).$ Now, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ -t \\ 2t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1+4t \\ 4-t \\ -2+2t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ And finally, the parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+4t \\ y=4-t \\ z=-2+2t\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equations of a Line
content.problem: Find the parametric equations of the line that passes through the points $P(1,4,-2)$ and $Q(5,3,0).$
content.worked_solution:
We know that the line passes through the points $P(1,4,-2)$ and $Q(5,3,0).$ Now, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ -t \\ 2t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1+4t \\ 4-t \\ -2+2t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ And finally, the parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=1+4t \\ y=4-t \\ z=-2+2t\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

Find the parametric equations of the straight line that passes through P(7,−11,3) and is parallel to v=⟨−3,2,7⟩.

a
{x=7+3ty=11+2tz=3−7t
b
{x=7−3ty=−11+2tz=3+7t
c
{x=7−3ty=−11−2tz=4+7t
d
{x=7+3ty=11−2tz=3+7t
e
{x=7+3ty=−11+2tz=3−7t
Submit

decision.explanation: Using r=P+tv gives (x,y,z)=(7,-11,3)+t(-3,2,7). Thus x=7-3t, y=-11+2t, and z=3+7t, matching option b.

after.name: Question 14
after.problem: Find the parametric equations of the straight line that passes through $P(7,-11,3)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨-3,2,7⟩.$
after.worked_solution:
First, the vector equation of the line is 

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -11 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -11 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3t \\ 2t \\ 7t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7-3t \\ -11+2t \\ 3+7t\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ Therefore, the parametric equations are:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=7-3t \\ y=-11+2t \\ z=3+7t\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

r=p+tvr=[7−113]+t[−327][xyz]=[7−113]+[−3t2t7t][xyz]=[7−3t−11+2t3+7t],

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option b: r=(7,-11,3)+t(-3,2,7), giving x=7-3t, y=-11+2t, z=3+7t. At t=0 it passes through P, and its direction vector is exactly v.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equations of a Line
content.problem: Find the parametric equations of the straight line that passes through $P(7,-11,3)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨-3,2,7⟩.$
content.worked_solution:
First, the vector equation of the line is 

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -11 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -11 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3t \\ 2t \\ 7t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7-3t \\ -11+2t \\ 3+7t\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ Therefore, the parametric equations are:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=7-3t \\ y=-11+2t \\ z=3+7t\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 15
after.problem: Find the parametric equations of the line that passes through the points $P(2,-5,4)$ and $Q(3,-2,2).$
after.worked_solution:
We need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}t \\ 3t \\ -2t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2+t \\ -5+3t \\ 4-2t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ And finally, the parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2+t \\ y=-5+3t \\ z=4-2t\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Find the parametric equations of the line that passes through the points $P(2,-5,4)$ and $Q(3,-2,2).$
content.worked_solution:
We need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}t \\ 3t \\ -2t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2+t \\ -5+3t \\ 4-2t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ And finally, the parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2+t \\ y=-5+3t \\ z=4-2t\end{aligned}
$$

First, we need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the line passing through the given points. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}t \\ t \\ -t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2+t \\ 1+t \\ -t\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

To get the equations for the line segment, we take only $t\in [0,1].$ Notice that substitution of $t=0$ in the above equation gives the coordinates of $P$ and substitution of $t=1$ gives the coordinates of $Q.$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ}$ are the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=2+t \\ y=1+t \\ z=-t\end{aligned}\,\,t\in [0,1]
$$
